cards.title: Structural vs. Practical Identifiability and FIM Diagnostics
cards.claim: Global structural identifiability means unique parameter solutions given ideal input-output data; local structural identifiability can allow finitely many alternatives. The source examines continuity and limiting behavior of the FIM determinant as diagnostic conditions in its fixed- and mixed-effects examples. A full-rank local FIM or these diagnostic conditions do not by themselves prove global structural uniqueness. Practical identifiability depends on imperfect data and study design. When the information-matrix approximation is applicable and the FIM is nonsingular, diagonal elements of its inverse provide approximate parameter variances and their square roots provide approximate standard errors; these are not guaranteed achieved precision.
conditions: Applicable to fixed- and mixed-effects PK/PD models.
Requires a defined design (time points) and parameter set.
Assumes the model structure is fixed during assessment.
required_inputs: Software capable of computing FIM or optimal design metrics (e.g., PFIM, PopED).
limitations: FIM diagnostics are local and design-specific; they do not prove global identifiability across all possible designs.
Numerical accuracy issues can cause unidentifiable models to show small positive determinants instead of zero.
Random effects identifiability does not always mirror fixed effects identifiability.
This is a diagnostic tool, not a proof of scientific validity or model correctness.
cards.downstream_use: Use to screen candidate models for structural identifiability before data collection. Use to evaluate if a proposed sampling schedule provides sufficient information (practical identifiability) to estimate parameters with acceptable precision.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Residual and censored observation models and structural/practical identifiability

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
